title: Understanding Model Risk
text: Model risk is calculated as the sum of the squared bias, the variance, and the squared standard deviation of the noise. Can you write down this formula?

title: Breaking Down the Formula
text: The formula for model risk is: risk $$=$$ $${bias}^2$$ + variance + standard $${deviation}^2$$. You know the bias and variance values. Can you substitute them into the formula?

title: Solving for Standard Deviation
text: After substituting the known values, you should have: $$38$$ $$=$$ $$5^2$$ + $$4$$ + standard $${deviation}^2$$. Can you solve for the standard deviation?

title: Calculate the Bias Squared
text: What is the value of bias squared if the bias is 5?

title: Substitute Known Values
text: Substitute the known values into the risk formula: $$38$$ $$=$$ $${bias}^2$$ + variance + standard $${deviation}^2$$. What is the equation after substitution?

title: Solve for Standard Deviation
text: Solve the equation $$38$$ $$=$$ $$25$$ + $$4$$ + standard $${deviation}^2$$ for the standard deviation. What is the standard deviation?
